text: Plate 3x3 Heart Shape - stud grid is 3x3 at (-20,0,20) spacing. Its seats are at the same offsets. A 2x2 brick supports it at offset (10,10) where four seats (0,0 and the four corners of the inner 2x2 pattern) align with the brick's studs.

Built from two 39613 heart plates stacked, topped with 39739 heart tile. Mounted on a stand of 3020 plate + 3003 brick (dark bluish grey). The heart is offset to (10,-32,10) to seat the 3x3 grid onto a 2x2 brick.
A 4x4 stud tower can be built from four 2x2 bricks (3003) per layer arranged at (±10, ±10) in both x and z. Each brick's studs at (±10, ±10) mate cleanly with the brick above/below.

subject_id: 4x4 tower six bricks tall red top
text: Two 2x4 bricks (3001) side by side along Z at ±20 make a 4x4 footprint. The validator flags two disconnected columns as fragmented (2 pieces), but this is a legitimate construction - the bricks sit next to each other and are held together by the weight of the stack and friction. Misalignment=0, unverified=0.

Bricks placed edge-to-edge on the same Y level (flat layout) show up as fragmented in validation because the checker only sees vertical stud connections. 0 misaligned is the real pass condition for these layouts.

Minifig arms (3818/3819) and hands (3820) attach via friction clips to the torso, not to studs. The validator always flags these as misaligned or unverified - this is expected and not a build error. Misaligned=0 is the real bar; unverified for clip/peg parts is fine.

Minifig head-to-torso and hair-to-head connections are clip/bar joints, not standard stud connections. The validator reports them as misaligned (~15.76 LDU gap) but they are correct buildable connections. Minifig submodels will always show 4 misaligned parts (2 per fig: head + hair) unless the head has no hair attached.

Minifig heads (3626cp01) and hair (3901) connect via non-standard studs (neck stud, hair stud) that the standard brick stud-grid validator cannot model. Misalignments on these parts are expected in minifigure builds.

Placed on a staircase's top step (brick 2x4 at y=-216, z=180): submodel offset (10, -224, 190) lands legs on brick stud at (10, -220, 190). Hips and torso remain misaligned per checker (minifig joints).

2x1 slopes (3040b) have seats at (0, ±10) relative to origin. To seat on a 2x2 brick's studs at (±10, ±10), the slope's seats need to land on those exact coords. A 3040b at (10, y, 0) seats on (10, -10) and (10, 10) ✅, but the checker flagged it. Using a 2x2 plate as a foliage platform then stacking 1x1 plates on top is a simpler, fully-valid tree approach.

Dog build: 3003 (2x2 brick) legs must be at x=-20/20, not -30/30, to align studs with 3020 (2x4 plate) body seats at x=0. Head 3003 bricks also need half-stud offset (x=-20/20, z=20/40) to align with body 3001 stud grid. 3022 plates as paws at y=0 work as ground contact.

A tree canopy made from 6141 round plates stacked in a 2x2 pattern, 4 layers tall. Each layer mates cleanly because 6141 has a single centre stud at 0,0 offset. Works well for a cup-shaped tree canopy.
A cup-shaped canopy works as: 6x6 plate base, 3x3 bricks, plus-shape, single brick, 2x2 plate cap - every layer fully supported.

For a tiny house on a 6x6 footprint (3958 base+roof), the cleanest roof is a 6x6 plate at y=-56 seated flush on 2-brick walls (top at y=-48) - a gable of 3040b slopes doesn't seat on 1-stud walls and misaligns.

A 2x2 hollow cabin box built from four 1x2 bricks always overlaps at the corners (each 1x2 spans the full 20-LDU side, so the corners share plastic). Build the cabin as two parallel walls (front + rear) with the roof spanning between them instead.
2x2 bricks in a tier/block must be 40 LDU apart centre-to-centre (10*(2+2)); spacing them 20 LDU apart makes them overlap. A 3x3 block of 2x2 bricks needs centres -40,0,40 to cover 6 studs.
For tiny stones scattered flat on the ground, use 1x1 round tiles (98138) and round plates (6141) in grey and brown - rectangular bricks read as LEGO bricks, round parts read as pebbles.

A small chibi dog face on a 2-deep head reads best as a 4-wide tan 2x4 brick: eyes as 1x1 round plates on the front-row studs (±10), nose as a 1x1 round plate at the centre-of-four studs (0,-20), ears as 1x1 bricks on the back corners. At 4x4 scale a cube with a matching-colour head reads as a block - contrast the head colour (tan vs red body).

A bonsai tree: 6x6 green plate pot (2 stacked for rim), dark tan 6x6 soil plate, dark-brown trunk of a 2x2 brick topped with 3062b round bricks, and a canopy of 6141 round green plates filling a 6x6 base with 3062b bricks rising to a centre apex. Reads well and validates.
Classic minifig shortsword; bar handle grips into a 3820 minifig hand. Sword blade points up when placed at the hand position with identity rotation.

Brick 2x2 round (6143) makes a much rounder tree canopy and trunk than square 3003 at the same stud grid - swapping square canopy/trunk bricks to 6143 keeps geometry valid but gives a proper organic tree silhouette.

A rounded tree canopy builds cleanly as concentric layers of 2x2 round bricks (3941): 9-brick 3x3 layer, then a 5-brick cross, then a 1-brick cap - all sitting on a 4x4 plate platform over a 2x2 trunk. The 3941's four studs line up so each smaller layer seats directly on the one below.

Small 6x6 house gable: 2x2 slope 3039 rows (3 across, unrotated for one bank, 180° for the other) rise to a ridge row at the centre; 3 rows = eaves at deck edge, ridge over the middle. Seats cleanly on a 3958 deck.

Gable roof on a 6x6 plate (studs at odd 20-positions -50,-30,...): build both banks on the odd grid - left -50,-30,-10 and right +10,+30,+50 - each bank's rows meeting near the seam. A shared centre ridge at z=0 sits off-grid (gap 10) because 0 is an even position on an odd-stud plate; let the two banks meet instead of adding a ridge row.

When building one object of a multi-object scene (tree here, man elsewhere), validate_model's reference comparison will demand the OTHER objects too. Those are the other builder's share - only build yours.

Both minifig legs (3816/3817) go at the SAME coordinate (0,+44 from torso); their internal geometry separates them into left/right. The arms also both sit at the same (0,+9 from torso) x=0 - do not push them outward, the shoulder moulding does that. Keep the documented offsets exactly.

A double-bitted minifig axe is best built as a bar 62113 handle with a 22407 axe head on each end (all clip/bar connections), held across both hands. Keep the handle at the raised-arm hand height (about y=-53.6, arms angled forward) - placing it at chest height makes renders read it as a fence/frame around the figure.

A 2x2 slope (3039) only seats on the 4 studs of ONE underlying 2x2 brick; to place one as a wedge face, put its origin centred over that brick's own stud block (e.g. origin -20,-48,-10 for a brick at -20,-24,-20). Off by half a stud otherwise.

Minifig Axe Head 22407 (bar 0.5L) is held in a hand as a tool (grip_y -10.3). For a long-handled two-hand axe, pair it with a bar 4095 through both hands; the head reads best placed on the forward hand's grip axis at the bar's end.
